maya (support): :rotating_light: Hey team — multiple customers reporting 502/504 and timeouts from the hosted inference API since ~10:20 PDT. Escalations piling in, two enterprise customers hit hard. I can share sample request IDs.
kevin (eng-oncall): Acknowledged. I'm jumping in. Can you paste a repro request ID + the raw curl so we can start tracing? @anika FYI.
maya (support): Sample: req=hdc-90b2fa. Customer used streaming chat endpoint with a long context (~6k tokens). Here's their curl:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-large-4k","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"<long history>"}],"stream":true}'
```
anika (sre): Thanks. Early signals from gateway logs show a surge in downstream 502s from the runtime pool around 10:18-10:22. Queue depth spiked and connection resets visible. Pushing logs.
incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1910004321 - "hosted api downstream timeouts". Pager on-call notified.
kevin (eng-oncall): Running quick check on the serving autoscaler and pool health. Sam — can you check KV/cache eviction and memory OOMs on the redwood-large-4k variant?
sam (runtime): Looking. I see a cluster of inference pods with elevated memory pressure and OOMKill events around 10:19 for a quantized 8-bit worker group. Also some RPC latency climbing between gateway -> runtime.
kevin (eng-oncall): That matches the connection resets. Likely one of two: either a bad model change pushed earlier that increased memory usage, or a burst of large-context streaming requests causing eviction thrashing. Did we do any model rollouts last deploy window?
garrett (product): We did push a model table update to add a new fallback variant at 03:00 UTC but no runtime image changes. No config changes scheduled this morning.
maya (support): Customers say it happened after their first streaming attempt. Most see 504 stream timeouts, some 502 gateway. A couple report retries causing client-side duplicate charges (billing concern).
billing-bot: Noted: flagging impacted customer accounts for refund review. Billing team alerted.
anika (sre): Short-term mitigation options: 1) Drain the overloaded runtime pool and spin new instances with higher memory headroom. 2) Enable immediate fallback routing to a lower-memory model variant for streaming requests. 3) Temporarily disable streaming for the redwood-large-4k for hosted tier while we stabilize.
kevin (eng-oncall): Let's do #2 + #1. Sam, can you flip routing fallback and scale up the pool by +30%? Also set a stricter circuit-breaker threshold for streaming requests to avoid queue amplification.
sam (runtime): Applying routing change now: updating routing policy to prefer redwood-medium-compat for requests with context > 4k tokens and for streams if runtime latency > 200ms. Scaling pool +35% now. I will also raise EVICT thresholds to avoid immediate OOM cascade.
kevin (eng-oncall): Patching gateway rule to add model fallback and lowering in-flight limit from 80 -> 48 for streaming per connection.
incident-bot: Config-change logged by kevin: PATCH /gateway/routing at 2026-03-15T17:31:42Z
maya (support): After the fallback flip a bunch of customer errors dropped — volume of 5xxs decreased ~75% in the last 4 minutes. Still seeing some stragglers.
kevin (eng-oncall): Good. I’m keeping pool scaling and watching for flapping. Sam, can you gather the OOM logs and the kernel messages for the killed processes? Need to confirm root cause.
sam (runtime): Pasted sample from worker node rn-14:
```
[10:19:21] python[pid=3421]: MemoryError during forward pass
[10:19:22] kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 3421 (runtime-worker) score 987
[10:19:23] kubelet: Killing container with id docker://runtime-worker due to OOMKilled
```
anika (sre): Node metrics show swap frenzy and CPU steal on some hosts — likely multi-tenancy contention + big-context streams. We should pin heavy models to dedicated allocations vs shared pool.
kevin (eng-oncall): Action for now: keep fallback routing active, scaled pool until traffic normalizes. I'll start a canary rollout to restrict large-context streaming to dedicated customer pools to prevent cross-tenant impact.
garrett (product): We'll need a customer communication: quick status + mitigation + timeline for permanent fix. @maya can you draft a short note to impacted customers saying we applied temporary fallbacks and are investigating root cause.
maya (support): Drafting now. Short note: "We identified intermittent timeouts affecting streaming chat. We applied routing fallbacks and scaled capacity; behavior should be improved. We're investigating root cause and will follow up with a permanent fix and any billing adjustments." Will send once you approve.
kevin (eng-oncall): Approve.
incident-bot: Incident status -> mitigated (reduced error rate) at 2026-03-15T17:36:10Z. Monitoring.
---
kevin (eng-oncall): Post-incident notes (starting thread follow-up): We mitigated with fallback routing + scaling. Preliminary root cause hypothesis: sudden burst of large-context streaming requests caused memory pressure on a subset of runtime nodes (quantized model variant produced larger transient memory use than expected), leading to OOM kills and downstream 502s. Contributing factors: shared pool pinning policy allowed heavy-model workloads on general-purpose hosts; circuit-breaker thresholds were too permissive for streaming.
anika (sre): Repro steps we used:
1) Send a streaming request with ~6k token history to redwood-large-4k concurrently from 40 clients.
2) Monitor runtime memory and kernel logs. Observe OOM within 2-3 minutes on a stressed node.
Repro curl (non-streaming simplified):
```
for i in {1..40}; do \
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -d '{"model":"redwood-large-4k","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"<6k tokens>"}],"stream":true}' &
done
```
sam (runtime): Logs to attach: /var/log/runtime/oom-2026-03-15.log, gateway-proxy-2026-03-15.log, prometheus snapshots for node metrics.
kevin (eng-oncall): Action items (owner, ETA):
- sam: Pin heavy models (redwood-large-4k) to dedicated pool and add node selectors for high-memory hosts. ETA: 48h
- anika: Update circuit-breaker defaults for streaming (lower inflight and faster failover). ETA: 24h
- eng-runtime: Add a telemetry alert for aggregate streaming memory usage across pool so we detect this before OOM. ETA: 7 days
- product (garrett) + support (maya): Customer follow-ups and credits review. ETA: 24h for initial comms, 72h for final reconciliation.
- kevin: Run an offline mem-profiling of the quantized path to see regression vs previous baseline. ETA: 72h
- ops: Review autoscaler rules to avoid slow scale-ups for bursty streaming traffic. ETA: 5 days
maya (support): Filed a ticket per impacted account and set holds for billing until postmortem done.
billing-bot: Marked three enterprise accounts for manual review and provisional credits.
garrett (product): We'll schedule a cross-functional postmortem meeting tomorrow to assign verification steps. Also need an RFC for long-term: model placement policy + streaming SLO guardrails.
kevin (eng-oncall): One immediate prevention I'm pushing: in gateway config, enforce a streaming-size check that rejects streams with >8k tokens (soft reject with 429) until the dedicated pools are live. That reduces blast radius.
anika (sre): I'll own the postmortem doc. Will include timeline, system traces, RCA, and detailed mitigation + test plan.
kevin (eng-oncall): Thanks all. Closing thread for live ops; continue follow-up in postmortem doc and scheduled meeting. I'll leave the fallback rules for another 30m then roll back if stable. If error rate increases, re-open incident.
maya (support): Sent customer updates. A few already replied that behavior improved. :thumbsup:
sam (runtime): Uploading logs and memprofile artifacts to the incident folder now.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-1910004321 status: monitoring -> resolved (provisional) at 2026-03-15T17:52:05Z
kevin (eng-oncall): Postmortem TODOs assigned above. Please add any missing items in the doc. We'll reconvene after initial RCA is posted.
